html:
The conquest of the northwest of the Indian subcontinent by the Achaemenid Persian Empire, completed under Darius I around 518 BCE.

Cyrus the Great had already taken lands west of the Indus around 535 BCE. Darius took Gandhara, around today's Peshawar and Taxila, and then the Indus valley itself, which the Persians called Hindush. His inscriptions, among them the Behistun inscription, list these lands among his provinces, or satrapies. He also sent a Greek sailor, Scylax, to explore the Indus down to the sea.

According to Herodotus, India paid the largest tribute of any province, in gold dust. Indian soldiers marched with Xerxes against Greece.

Persian rule lasted almost two centuries and left a mark. Persian officials wrote in Aramaic, and from Aramaic letters grew the Kharosthi script used in the northwest for centuries. Persian ideas of kingship and stone inscriptions may have shaped the later Maurya emperors. The region passed to Alexander at the Hydaspes in 326 BCE.
sum: The conquest of the northwest of the Indian subcontinent by the Achaemenid Persian Empire, completed under Darius I around 518 BCE.
